transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because my communication has been really off lately. People keep telling me they can’t follow what I’m trying to explain. 

It's happening a lot with my work. Like, my artist statements, my notes for clients, and even just what I say out loud in meetings. I guess my thoughts just jump around too much. I'll go from talking about the textures of a piece to the budgets, and then straight into these... secret meanings behind it all. It makes sense in my head at the time, but it's getting really hard to do my job when no one can understand what I'm saying.
Is this jumping between ideas something that happens to you all the time, or is it a relatively new development?

It hasn't been happening my whole life. It's been going on for about... I'd say a year and two months now. That's right around the time I switched from doing community curation into full-time independent installation work.
Have you been experiencing any unusual perceptions, like hearing or seeing things that others don't, or beliefs that seem real to you but others find strange?

Yeah, actually, I have noticed some things like that. Um, mostly when I’m alone in my studio. I’ll sometimes hear a woman quietly commenting on things... it usually sounds like it's coming from behind the storage shelves. 

And sometimes I'll smell things, too, like the strong scent of hot metal right near an unfinished piece. It feels completely real when it happens. I always stop what I'm doing and go check to see who's there or what's burning, but... there’s never anyone around, and nothing is actually there.
Do you think the woman's comments or the smells you experience are trying to tell you something specific or convey a particular message?

I don't know if the voice or the smells are trying to tell me something, exactly. But I do get these... well, I get convinced that other things are sending me messages. 

Like, I'll notice certain stains in the studio, or the way seams line up on a piece, or even just specific phrases in emails from galleries, and I feel absolutely sure they are meant specifically for me. It feels like they are instructions, or maybe warnings about my work. And it's really hard to let go of that idea once it's in my head. Even when someone shows me a completely ordinary explanation for what the gallery meant, or why a stain is there, I just... I still can't shake the feeling that it's a hidden message just for me.
Do these messages and warnings you feel like you're receiving from various things seem to be related to each other in some way?

Um, I don't think so. I haven't really noticed them connecting to each other. It's not like... well, I don't feel like there's one big puzzle tying it all together, if that's what you mean. 

The email from the gallery might feel like one specific warning about a show, and then the stain on the studio floor is just a totally different instruction about how to build a piece. They don't really seem related to each other at all. They just... they both just feel very urgent and meant specifically for me in that exact moment.
Are these experiences, such as hearing the woman's comments or feeling like you're receiving hidden messages, causing you a lot of distress or anxiety?

Um, not really, no. I wouldn't say they cause me a lot of distress or make me panic. It's more just... distracting, I guess? 

Like, when I hear the voice or smell the metal, I just stop what I'm doing to check it out. And the messages... they feel important when I notice them, but they don't really scare me or make me super anxious. It's just kind of something that happens while I'm working.
Are you having trouble completing tasks or meeting deadlines at work due to these experiences?

Well, yes, actually. It has been affecting my work quite a bit. I've missed some paid deadlines because I get so caught up in the messages or distracted by the other things. And in meetings, I've ended up really confusing my collaborators because of it. It got to the point where an exhibition had to be postponed recently... my notes and proposals just stopped making enough sense for them to use.
Do you feel like all these messages and warnings are part of something bigger that you're trying to understand?

No, not really a bigger picture. Like I mentioned, they don't really seem connected to each other. It's more just that... I get completely convinced that these individual things—like certain stains on the floor, or the seams on something, or just a specific phrase in a gallery email—are meant specifically for me. 

They just feel exactly like direct instructions or warnings about my work. And it is very hard to let go of that. Even when someone else looks at it and shows me a completely ordinary explanation for the stain or what the email meant, I still can't really shake the feeling that it was a message for me.
Are these experiences affecting your relationships with friends and family?

No, not really. I mean, I don't really talk to my family much anyway, and my friends... well, I haven't noticed it causing any big issues with them. I guess I've just been keeping to myself a bit more lately because of work stuff, but it's not like we're fighting or anything.
Do you find that your thoughts are often disjointed or hard to follow, even when you're not trying to communicate them to someone else?

Yeah, I do. That's actually the main reason I came in to see someone. My thoughts just kind of... scatter. Even when I'm just trying to work things out in my head, but it's really obvious when I try to write or talk. My artist statements, the notes I write for clients, even what I say in meetings... I'll start talking about the texture of a piece, and then suddenly I'm talking about the budget, and then about the secret meanings in the materials. People keep telling me they just can't follow what I'm trying to explain. It's like my brain just jumps from one thing to another without any real connection.
Do you feel like there's an underlying idea or theme that connects all these messages and experiences you're having?

I think I mentioned this just a minute ago, but no, not really. There isn't an underlying theme connecting them all. It's more just... isolated things. 

Like I was saying, I'll see a random stain, or a seam, or read a specific phrase in an email from a gallery, and I just become absolutely convinced it's a direct instruction or a warning meant specifically for me and my art. And the hardest part is that even if someone sits down and shows me a totally normal, logical explanation for the email or the spill, I still can't let it go. I just can't shake that feeling that it was a message for me.
Do you feel like all these messages and experiences are part of a single, overarching idea or story that makes sense to you?

I think you might have just asked me something similar, actually. But no, there's no big story or single idea connecting them. 

It's exactly like I just described—just those isolated moments. I'll see a stain, or a seam, or read a phrase in a gallery email, and I just get completely convinced it's a specific instruction or a warning about my work. They don't link together into a plot. The main issue is just that when it happens, it's incredibly hard to let it go, even when someone gives me a completely ordinary explanation for it.
Do you feel like these messages and experiences are all part of a coherent story or belief system that makes sense to you?

I'm sorry, but I feel like you're asking me the exact same thing again. Like I just explained, no, there is no big story or system to it. 

It's literally just what I was saying—I get convinced that certain stains, seams, or phrases in gallery emails are instructions or warnings meant specifically for me and my art. And it's just very hard to let go of that belief even when someone shows me a completely ordinary explanation. That's really all there is to it. They don't link together into anything bigger.
Are you noticing any effects from these experiences in your daily routines outside of work?

Well, honestly, the biggest impact hasn't really been outside of work—it's been on my actual art career. I've missed paid deadlines because of all this. And when I have meetings, I just end up confusing my collaborators. It's gotten to the point where I actually had an exhibition postponed recently, mostly because my notes and my project proposals just stopped making enough sense for anyone to use.
Do you feel like these messages and experiences are all connected to a central idea that you're trying to uncover or understand?

I... okay, I really feel like we are just going in circles here. You keep asking me this exact same question. 

No, there is no central idea or big mystery I'm trying to uncover. Like I've been saying, it's just those isolated things. I'll see a stain, or a seam, or a certain phrase in a gallery email, and I get absolutely convinced that it's an instruction or a warning meant specifically for me about my art. And it's just very hard to let that go, even when someone shows me a completely ordinary explanation for it. But they aren't connected to anything bigger than that.
Do you find it difficult to stay on topic when speaking or writing, even when you're not trying to convey complex ideas about your art?

Yeah, actually, that's... that's exactly why I came in. It's not just when I'm trying to explain complicated art concepts. Even my basic artist statements or, like, notes for clients have gotten really messy. I'll be talking in a meeting, and I'll jump from talking about the texture of a piece, straight into budget stuff, and then into those hidden meanings I mentioned. People keep telling me they just can't follow what I'm trying to explain anymore. It's like my thoughts are just skipping around too fast for anyone else to keep up.
Have you noticed any changes in your behavior or daily activities that seem disorganized or hard to manage?

Yeah, I have. It's... well, it's definitely getting hard to manage. There are days where I'll just spend an hour moving the same tools into tiny rows on my workspace. Or I'll catch myself tracing the exact same square in the air, over and over. Sometimes I just pace around an installation instead of actually building the piece. And the frustrating part is, I do all of this even though I know my deadline is slipping.
Do you feel like your disorganized thoughts and behaviors are causing you significant emotional distress?

Yes, it's incredibly stressful. It's actually messing up my livelihood at this point. I've missed paid deadlines because I'm just pacing or arranging my tools instead of working. And like I said, I've confused my collaborators in meetings because I can't stay on track. I even had a gallery exhibition postponed recently because my proposals and the notes I sent them just... they stopped making enough sense for the gallery to use. So, yeah, it's causing a lot of problems for me.
Are there times when you engage in repetitive behaviors or movements without any voices or messages telling you to do so?

No, not really. I mean, the repetitive stuff I mentioned—like lining up my tools or tracing shapes in the air—that just happens. There aren't any voices or messages telling me to do it. It's just... something I catch myself doing.
Do you think your thoughts and the way you express them are the main problems you're experiencing?

Yeah, I think they are. I mean, that's actually the main reason I came in. My artist statements, the notes I write for clients, and even just what I say in meetings... they've started jumping all over the place. I'll be talking about textures, and then suddenly I'm on budgets, or... or some secret meaning behind the piece. People just keep telling me they can’t follow what I’m trying to explain. So, yeah, the way I'm expressing myself is definitely a big part of the problem.

I'll be talking about textures, and then suddenly I'm on budgets, or... or some secret meaning behind the piece. People just keep telling me they can’t follow what I’m trying to explain. So, yeah, the way I'm expressing myself is definitely a big part of the problem.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of disorganized thinking, speech, and behavior, along with the presence of hallucinations and delusions, are consistent with a diagnosis of unspecified schizophrenia spectrum disorder.
